review: reviewer: agree: prayer reading (may they grant) is the natural one for an invocation
reviewer: agree: बिधि as address 'O Creator' is the plain reading
reviewer: agree: सनाथ = having found my master/Lord; keep

issue: No verb in 'bhaktipradau tau hi naḥ': statement ('are givers of devotion to us') or prayer ('may they give')
our reading: prayer: may those two indeed grant us devotion
alternatives: those two indeed are the givers of devotion to us

issue: बिधि in 'करिहहिं बिधि मो सन ए प्रीती': address to the Creator, or 'in this way / by any means'
our reading: address: O Creator, will these two show me love?
alternatives: will these two love me in this way?

issue: सनाथ: 'having a master/protector' (attaining the Lord) or 'fulfilled, blessed'
our reading: I shall have found my Lord (सनाथ हो जाऊँगा)

review: Agree: the plain reading (the four, the daughter included, are alike) is right and is what the meaning gives; keep the doubt for the owner.
Agree: निज धाम kept as ambiguous as the verse; Gita Press's Hindi adds परम.
Agree with the doubt; the Hindi "फल देकर" leans on the alternative a little but stays within "सुहाए"; acceptable until the owner decides.

issue: कन्या सम ए चारी: "these four are alike" or "these (three) are like a daughter".
our reading: A younger brother's wife, a sister, a son's wife and a daughter: these four are alike.
alternatives: The younger brother's wife, the sister and the son's wife are to be regarded as a daughter (ए चारी then counting the daughter as the standard).

issue: निज धाम: Śrī Rāma's own abode or Vāli's own (proper) abode.
our reading: Kept as ambiguous as the verse: "his own abode" / "अपने धाम".
alternatives: Gita Press reads Rāma's supreme abode (परम धाम).

issue: पाइ समय जिमि सुकृत सुहाए: what "सुहाए" means for merits.
our reading: Good deeds shine out (bear fruit) when their time comes.
alternatives: Merits appear / come forward at the right time.

review: Agree with the writer's doubt and reading (knowing the work would be done by him); no change needed.

issue: जानि काज: what the Lord 'knew' about the work is not stated.
our reading: knowing the work would be done by him (Hanumān)

review: Agree: कहहिं may be Jāmbavān (honorific plural, continuing 26.cau6, where he told the tale) or the monkeys; the impersonal rendering is a safe plain reading. Keep the doubt for the owner.
Agree: गरुड़ as Kākabhuśuṇḍi's address to Garuḍa is the usual reading; keep as is, doubt recorded.

issue: Subject of कहहिं (plural): Jāmbavān (honorific, continuing 26.cau6) or the monkeys talking among themselves.
our reading: Left impersonal: the tale was being told in many ways.
alternatives: the monkeys were talking in many ways

issue: गरुड़ read as Kākabhuśuṇḍi addressing Garuḍa, beside गीध (the vulture).
alternatives: an epithet of the vulture Sampāti
